clue.text: Accidentally reveal one is freely available?

definitions.meaning: to let slip your true feelings or a secret without meaning to
read literally, handing yourself over for nothing, as if you were a free gift

explanation.surface: Someone lets slip a secret and wonders whether they now seem easy to obtain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to betray yourself unintentionally; read word by word it describes donating your own person.

clue.text: Death sentence widely publicised?

parts.note: a dying person's final utterance (a sentence at death) that becomes celebrated and widely quoted

explanation.surface: A news report of a court passing capital punishment that the press spreads everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Death sentence' suggests a judge's verdict, but here it is a sentence spoken at the moment of death, made famous.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names celebrated dying utterances, and is used ironically for confident remarks soon proved wrong.

clue.text: Watch and record celebrity welcome

parts.note: ticker is slang for a watch (or a heart)
to tape something is to record it

explanation.surface: Someone sees and films a star's grand arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticker-tape parade, with paper strips thrown from windows, is the classic New York welcome for heroes and stars.

clue.text: Directs rising model to enter, this far ahead?

indicators.note: the model letter is told to go inside the word for directs
in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to direct a vehicle is to steer it, so directs means steers
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: An instruction to a fashion model who is moving up in the world, asking if they are well in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts T inside STEERS to make STEERTS, and 'rising' turns that upwards into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'streets ahead' is a British idiom for being far in front, so the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: Nuclear reactor is a singular source of discomfort

definitions.meaning: an atomic ... was the early term for a nuclear reactor
haemorrhoids; one of them, in the singular

explanation.surface: A power station is described as a uniquely annoying presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular' looks like 'remarkable', but it means grammatically singular: one of the painful piles.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an early atomic reactor and, in the plural, haemorrhoids; the singular form covers one of them.

clue.text: Bewildering situation, as recurring itches need treatment

indicators.note: the itches are to be treated, worked on until the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: A confusing medical case where persistent itching keeps needing a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus with three rings running acts at once is a figure for chaotic, confusing goings-on.

clue.text: Composition of contemporary youth

definitions.meaning: the title of Michael Tippett's 1940s oratorio
a young person belonging to the present era

explanation.surface: An essay written about today's young people.
explanation.definitionFit: Tippett's oratorio bears this title, and the words literally describe a youngster of the current age.

clue.text: Closed hand around broken nail, one of only two left?

indicators.note: the clenched hand goes around the rearranged nail letters

parts.note: a fist is a closed hand

indicators.note: a broken nail is damaged, so its letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A fist clenched over a split fingernail, perhaps after a fight with just two survivors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' hints at a direction or a hand, but it means still remaining in a competition; 'broken' scrambles the nail and 'around' wraps the hand round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A finalist is one of the last two competitors left in a contest.

clue.text: Pub shortly has wine locked up

indicators.note: said briefly, so the word for pub loses its last letter

parts.note: an inn is a pub
hock is German white wine, from Hochheim

explanation.surface: A short pub description: there is wine kept under lock and key.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in hock means pawned, or in British slang in prison, so held and locked away.

clue.text: Applied to have role as a hobbit?

parts.note: to be someone in a play is to have that role
Took is a hobbit family in Tolkien, Pippin Took among them

explanation.surface: Someone auditions to play a hobbit in a Tolkien film.
explanation.definitionFit: To betake oneself to something is an old way of saying to go to it or apply oneself; the past tense fits applied.

clue.text: Critical interpretation of sacrifice of six geese

indicators.note: the geese are sacrificed, destroyed in their present form, so their letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A scholarly reading of a ritual slaughter of half a dozen geese.
explanation.definitionFit: Exegesis is the critical explanation of a text, especially scripture.

clue.text: African natives have information to announce

indicators.note: announcing is speaking out, so we want a word that sounds like the information

parts.note: news is information

explanation.surface: Local Africans are given some news to broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnus, or wildebeest, are antelopes native to Africa, so the natives are animals rather than people.

clue.text: Going back, regret road is up

indicators.note: something that is up is amiss or wrong, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Someone retraces a route and laments that the road is dug up.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrograde describes moving backwards or reverting to an earlier state.

clue.text: Pearly ring with faint odour

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
faint in colour is pale
scent is an odour

explanation.surface: A pearl ring giving off a faint smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Opalescent describes the milky, shimmering sheen of opal or pearl.

clue.text: One's cooler outside a hot city

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I'S, written IS

indicators.note: the cooler goes outside, around the following letters

parts.note: a fan cools the air
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A traveller's fan keeps them cool in a sweltering town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps FAN around A and H to give FAHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Isfahan is a historic city in central Iran, famous for its mosques.

clue.text: Failed to notice any females, in short …

parts.note: to fail to notice any is to have seen none, saw no
F is short for female; two of them are FF

explanation.surface: Someone who saw not a single woman, put briefly, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 18 across, whose words carry on the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawn-off gun or garment has been cut down, so it is shorter than usual.

clue.text: Journey in a ship covered by part of journal

indicators.note: the inner letters are enclosed by the page

parts.note: a journal is made of pages
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A sea voyage recorded on a page of a travel diary.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a journey, especially a voyage by sea.

clue.text: … none distinguished, anyway

definitions.meaning: if none stands out, each is identical to the others

explanation.surface: Continuing 16: no women seen, none of them noteworthy anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both identical to each other and nevertheless, as in 'thanks all the same'.

clue.text: Stroke, making murmuring sound

indicators.note: the word for murmuring is spoken out, giving a word heard the same

parts.note: a coo is the soft murmuring sound of a dove

explanation.surface: A stroke of the hand that produces a soft cooing.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a sudden successful stroke, as in a masterstroke or coup d'état.

clue.text: Look into deep cuts in protective wear

indicators.note: the look word goes into the cuts

parts.note: gashes are deep cuts
lo is an old word meaning look, as in 'lo and behold'

explanation.surface: A doctor examines serious wounds sustained despite safety clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Galoshes are rubber overshoes worn to protect shoes from wet and mud.

clue.text: Tuft that is missing from tissue

indicators.note: the abbreviation is taken away from the tissue word

parts.note: a hankie is a handkerchief, often a paper tissue
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A tuft of fibre is missing from a paper hankie.
explanation.definitionFit: A hank is a coil or tuft of yarn, hair or wool.

clue.text: One given orders to prepare exhibition

definitions.meaning: a priest's assistant who has taken holy orders
to select and arrange items for a museum show

explanation.surface: A soldier commanded to set up a display.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is an assistant parish priest in holy orders; the verb is to organise a show.

clue.text: Head of college endlessly excited by study

indicators.note: without its end, so the excited word loses its final letter

parts.note: warm can mean ardent or excited
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A college principal who never stops getting worked up about research.
explanation.definitionFit: Some Oxford colleges call their head the Warden.

clue.text: Spirit doubly applied to my game

parts.note: the word spirit is used twice over, for two spirits: gin and then rum

explanation.surface: Someone adds two shots of liquor to their party game.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin rummy is a two-player card game, a version of rummy.
